text.p: Italian debt markets ended the day in the red after a choppy session in low volumes ahead of a four-day Easter weekend in most of Europe except for Italy.
Italian markets are open Friday but closed on Monday, while LIFFE is shut for both days.

Dealers here said lower U.S. t-bonds and other markets' losses had weighed on Btps. The November 2006 Btp closed 42 basis points down at 100.68, with the yield 7.78 percent and the spread over the 10-year Bund 185 basis points.
The June LIFFE future was 63 basis points off at 124.75.

The government unveiled the details of its additional budget deficit cutting measures for this year designed to squeeze Italy into the parameters required for joining a European single currency at its projected 1999 start.

Economists say its going to be a tight fit however, with Credito Italiano economists predicting the real effect of the 15.5 trillion lire package will only be 13.1 trillion by the year end, giving Italy a deficit to GDP ratio of 3.1 percent rather than spot on the 3.0 percent required for EMU.
The package aims at 6.0 trln from advance tax on severance pay and 4.2 trillion from altering tax payment systems.
The rest of the cash will be brought in by ministerial spending cuts and by imposing a temporary block on state workers drawing early retirement handouts.
It brought few surprises to the market as its contents had been well flagged in the preceding days.
The lira held firmer than the 1,000 per mark barrier at 998.50/8.99 in late trade.
